title: Suspected Susac syndrome
consultQuestion: Encephalopathy or new headache with callosal lesions, hearing loss, or visual symptoms — Susac rather than MS?
keyHistory: New cognitive or behavioral change, focal symptoms, or new migrainous/oppressive headache preceding other features by ≤6 months (Kleffner Box 1)
New tinnitus, hearing loss, or peripheral vertigo (Kleffner Box 1)
Visual symptoms are often absent — visual impairment reported in 28% though 58% had field defects (Kleffner)
Prior MS diagnosis or MS therapy — MS is the most common misdiagnosis; MS immunotherapy may worsen SuS (Kleffner)
keyExam: Funduscopy — branch retinal artery occlusions may be silent (Kleffner)
redFlags: Severe encephalopathy — can mask the other triad features (Kleffner)
Planned MS disease-modifying therapy in a patient who may have SuS (Kleffner)

clues: Complete triad at onset in only 13%
Callosal 'snowball' lesions; BRAO or arterial wall hyperfluorescence on FLA; low/mid-tone sensorineural hearing loss (Kleffner)
Most common misdiagnosis of SuS; intrathecal IgG/OCBs are rare in SuS (Kleffner)

notes: Required for brain criterion: multifocal round T2/FLAIR lesions with ≥1 in the corpus callosum ('snowball') (Kleffner Box 1)
Supportive only: T1-hypointense lesions, gray-matter lesions, leptomeningeal enhancement
Do it even without visual symptoms — BRAO may be silent (Kleffner Box 1)
BRAO or arterial wall hyperfluorescence (AWH; marker of activity) meets the retinal criterion
Required to support hearing loss; typically low/mid-tone sensorineural (Kleffner Box 1)

indication: Later disease, when FLA no longer shows BRAO/AWH
notes: Sectoral inner-retinal damage meets the retinal criterion (Kleffner)
Required to support vestibular vertigo (Kleffner Box 1)
Protein often raised; mild pleocytosis (median 12 cells) in 45%; intrathecal IgG/OCBs rare — not a criterion (Kleffner)

decisionRules.condition: Brain, retinal, and vestibulocochlear criteria all met
evidenceNote: European Susac Consortium criteria, Kleffner 2016 Box 1

decisionRules.condition: Two of the three criteria met
decisionRules.recommendation: Probable Susac syndrome — treat as definite and re-examine frequently

decisionRules.condition: Some features but fewer than two criteria
decisionRules.recommendation: Possible SuS — keep in the differential, follow closely
Neurological exam, brain MRI, ophthalmology exam with FLA, audiogram, and vestibular testing in every patient

initialSteps: Acute episode: high-dose corticosteroids; continuous immunosuppression to prevent relapses — no trials, empirical (Kleffner)
pearls: Complete triad at onset in only 13% (Kleffner)
Brain, muscle, and skin biopsies are nonspecific — diagnose with less invasive testing (Kleffner)
No specific serologic marker; anti-endothelial cell antibodies >1:100 in only 25% (Kleffner)
sources: Kleffner I, et al. Diagnostic criteria for Susac syndrome (European Susac Consortium). J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2016 (published online first Oct 25, 2016). doi:10.1136/jnnp-2016-314295
